goal: Run a single web search then synthesize a grounded answer — Arm C sanity floor regardless of task type.
rationale: One frozen linear shape: web_search -> synthesize. This is the simplest grounded graph that can be run against any task. Its purpose is the sanity floor: if the dynamic planner (Arm A) or the router library (Arm B) cannot beat a single-search linear shape on eval metrics, those arms have no value. The shape is intentionally unsophisticated. Both the search query and the synthesize instruction carry a {prompt} placeholder the bench harness literal-substitutes (str.replace, not str.format) with the task prompt before the run — the user's prompt never reaches DynamicRunState values on the real runner path, so without substitution the graph would run prompt-blind.

params.instruction: Using the web search results provided in upstream state (search_results), produce a direct, grounded answer to the user's original request: {prompt} Preserve key facts, numbers, and source references from the search results. Keep the answer concise and focused.

metadata.purpose: Arm C fixed sanity floor — single linear web_search -> synthesize
